question: Does an observed adjacent-agreement statistic expose the conditional-law mismatch that the original nested predictor scarcely detects?
outcome: On 1,000 fresh populations, broad vector references reject 94.2% at nominal 5%, compared with 1.0% for quality-conditioned references; paired difference 93.2 percentage points, interval 91.6–94.7. Exact conditional tails give 95.0% and .8%. All 198,000 references, 1,547 cell distributions and 2,000 exact tails pass independent replay. The original nested 4% versus 3% result remains preserved.
challenge: The statistic was developed after the nested main result. Integer ties and constant-score configurations make the matched reference conservative.
remedy: Freeze the new observed-sign statistic and fresh seed namespaces before generation, label it post-outcome method development, and verify the row-state dynamic program with a separate hypergeometric convolution.
retry_when: A new observable quality proxy, observation mechanism or separately specified statistic changes the sensitivity question.
